description.narrative: (Bangladesh): Youth comprise 35 percent of Bangladesh's population and have the potential to significantly contribute to Bangladesh's socio-economic success. Historically, youth have not been empowered to maximize their potential and continue to experience high unemployment (13.8 percent) due to lack of soft and technical skills. Traditional gender and social norms also hinder youth workforce participation across sectors. To address this, the USAID Bijoyee (Winner) activity will elevate youths' ability to effectively contribute to the economy and society. With FY 2024 funds, Bijoyee will provide youth with skills to better access economic opportunities and strengthen the organizational capacity of local youth and youth-led organizations to serve more youth in the future. This activity will equip youth with industry-demanded soft skills, increase their ability to better access wage and self-employment opportunities, increase youth participation in civic action, and support young Bangladeshis in their journey towards being global citizens. USAID will partner with the Government of Bangladesh and the private sector to transform the youth-serving ecosystem in line with localization principles and shift power to youth. Bijoyee will benefit youth from diverse backgrounds, prioritizing those not currently in education, employment, or training and encourage civic engagement and advocacy on topics such as addressing climate change and for changes to restrictive traditional gender and social norms. The activity aligns with CDCS DO Two and Three and ICS MO 3.1 Improved human capital, particularly in health and education. Funding will contribute to the Basic Education ($625,802) earmark with Girls in Areas of Conflict ($625,802), Gender Equality/Women's Empowerment - Secondary ($ 375k), Gender Based Violence ($250k), and Private Sector Engagement ($125,160) attributions.
